checks.label: A three-phase bridge gives a DC bus of approximately 1.35 × the line voltage: 1.35 × 400 V = 540 V, the link drawn here
One leg averages D × 540 V. At 60% depth D runs from 20% to 80%: 108 V at the trough, 270 V at the zero and 432 V at the peak
The amplitude of the phase voltage is determined by the duty cycle: each switching cycle's pulses are on for D of it, so they average D times the link, at every depth
H-bridge: the winding averages (2D − 1) × 540 V. At 50% depth and 90°, D is 75% and it sees 405 − 135 = 270 V, 191 V rms. At 60%, a 324 V peak and 229 V rms. At full depth, 382 V rms
Sine-triangle PWM works for three sine waves 120° out of phase: the three legs' references are drawn 120° apart, against one carrier
Three legs: between lines the average peaks at √3 × 270 = 468 V at full depth, 331 V rms. At 60% depth, 198 V rms
The motor filters the supplied current into a near-sine wave: with the fastest carrier, the drawn line current stays close to a sine
The sawtooth falls in proportion as the carrier rises: at 3 kHz it is about a third as tall as at 1 kHz, while the current stays a 50 Hz near-sine
One IGBT is always turned off first and the other turned on after the dead time, preventing a bridge shoot-through: only a dead time shorter than the turn-off lag draws one
Each gap costs the winding 2 × dead time × carrier frequency × 540 V against the current: about 22 V at 20 µs and 1 kHz, 108 V at 100 µs. The drawn pulses lose that much
The dead time causes distortion in the output current, so the smaller the dead time the better: with the longest gap the drawn current stalls near each zero, and with a short one it does not
Double conversion provides zero transfer time to battery: on the card the UPS inverter feeds the load all the time, from the DC link that holds the battery
Static conversion of the 50/60 Hz port grid power to match the 60/50 Hz vessel network: the shore chain runs from a 50 Hz port grid through rectifier, DC link and inverter to a 60 Hz vessel network
Each puzzle offers three answers and accepts only its right one, every wrong answer has its own hint, and hidden numbers appear only after a right Check
Each demonstration ends within 4.5 s of its screen opening, and a right answer shows within 3 s of Check
From the same 540 V link, a smaller depth narrows the pulses near the peak and shrinks the average sine: in the H-bridge at 90°, on for 80% at 60% depth and 65% at 30%, with peaks of 324 V and 162 V
